t: This is the East India Club at 16 St James's Square, a gentlemen's club founded in 1849. It was originally set up for officers of the East India Company, and its first patron was Prince Albert. Over the years its members have included royalty, senior military officers, politicians, diplomats and businessmen. Dorothy Elizabeth Boehm, who lived from 1766 to 1842, is recorded as having commissioned and owned the building, and she appears in the Legacies of British Slavery database.
